title: Laboratory Test Orders: Number of Orders a Patient May Hold
content:
A patient may hold any number of Laboratory Test Orders at the same time, in any service classes and in any statuses. Each accession is its own order, and nothing caps how many orders a patient holds.

## What this means at the desk

| Question about a patient's orders | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of orders per patient? | No. There is no per-patient maximum. |
| May the orders be in different service classes? | Yes, in any service classes. |
| May some be resulted while others are on hold or cancelled? | Yes, in any statuses at the same time. |
| Do two accessions count as one order? | No. Each accession is its own order. |

**Example (hypothetical).** A patient holds a resulted Routine Clinical Testing order, a Specialty Clinical Testing order still awaiting its specimen and a cancelled Clinical Toxicology Testing order. All three are separate orders held at the same time, and a further order in any class may be added alongside them.
